title: 2 caught cheating using AI glasses during college entrance exams
source_used: The Korea Times (full text read, 982 characters); details cross-checked in Korea JoongAng Daily and The Korea Herald
key_facts: Two college applicants were caught this month wearing banned AI glasses at entrance exams at two Seoul schools, sources said on Tuesday 13 Oct 2026 (Korea Times).

A Yonsei University applicant wore normal glasses before the mathematics essay portion on Saturday (10 Oct) and switched to AI glasses after the exam began; proctors reported the student, who admitted it; Yonsei is reviewing possible action.

At the University of Seoul on 3 Oct, an applicant wore regular glasses while supervisors checked IDs and switched to smart glasses later; the school removed the student and banned the applicant from its entrance exam for three years.
Korea JoongAng Daily calls the Yonsei case the first known case of AI smart-glasses cheating on a Korean university admissions test; 14,452 applicants competed for 288 places in that essay track.

Korea Herald (14 Oct) says Yonsei invalidated the student's results but has not yet restricted future exams because its rules do not specify such a penalty, and that the Education Ministry could discuss standardising penalties; it dates the Yonsei exam Friday where the Korea Times and JoongAng say Saturday.
Korea Herald explains that smart glasses can use cameras in the frames to photograph questions, process them with AI and show answers on the lenses.
quote_evidence: Two college applicants were caught cheating this month by wearing prohibited artificial intelligence (AI) glasses while taking college entrance exams at two different schools in Seoul, sources said Tuesday.
The University of Seoul immediately removed the student from the test site and banned the applicant from taking its entrance exam for the next three years.
Yonsei University is currently reviewing possible action against the examinee.
why_it_matters_hint: Camera-equipped AI glasses are now being used to cheat in high-stakes exams, and universities are punishing it unevenly.
event_date: 3 Oct and 10 Oct 2026 (Saturday); first reported 12-13 Oct 2026
notes: The Korea Times does not name its sources; Korea JoongAng Daily and the Korea Herald carry the same cases with university officials. The Herald dates the Yonsei exam Friday; the Korea Times and JoongAng say Saturday (10 Oct). The Korea Times text appears to be a wire text with the same wording as a JoongAng piece, but neither names an agency.
